title: Hardware modules and racks
summary: CPU, power supply and I/O modules in slots: how the configuration describes the installed hardware.

sections.heading: Slots and modules
sections.body: Modules sit in numbered **slots** of a rack or rail. The engineer configures which module type belongs in each slot. At startup and continuously, the CPU compares the configuration with what is really installed.

sections.heading: A small rack
sections.body: Slot numbers start at the CPU.
sections.diagram:
| slot 0 | slot 1        | slot 2        | slot 3       |

           %I0.0..%I0.7    %Q0.0..%Q0.7    %IW64..

sections.heading: Configuration is data
sections.body: In PLC Lab the station configuration lists modules, channel modes and the I/O map; the program only uses tags.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Swapping two modules of different types during maintenance. The CPU reports a configuration difference and the affected I/O delivers nothing.

question.question: The hardware view shows 'configured DI 8, installed DO 8' in slot 1. What happens to the inputs of slot 1?
question.explanation: A mismatched module does not exchange data.

sections.heading: Explore the hardware view
sections.body: Open any machine and inspect modules, LEDs, channel values and the multimeter in the Hardware tab.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
The hardware configuration describes modules per slot; mismatches are diagnosed by the CPU.

**Troubleshooting note:** Compare configured and installed modules first when several signals of one module fail at once.

checkpoint.question: What does the CPU compare at startup?
Several inputs of one module fail at once. First suspect?
